thread:
alicia: FYI — Acme's CISO just asked: if a breach affecting PII happens during a POC, what is Redwood's incident response timeline and when would we notify them? They want a short, clear answer for the RFP. cc @samir @maria

samir: Short answer: we aim to notify impacted customers with an initial investigatory notice within 72 hours of confirming a security incident. Internal IR starts immediately on detection. For POCs we treat them as production-adjacent; exact actions depend on hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated/private).

maria: Clarification: "notify" here should be defined in the RFP text as an "initial notification that we are investigating a potential security incident and what steps we're taking" — not the final root-cause report. Contract language varies; our DPA says "as soon as reasonably practicable," but operationally we default to 72h for regulated customers/regions (GDPR).

samir: IR flow (high level):
• Detection/alert -> Triage (scope & impact) -> Containment -> Forensics & log preservation -> Remediation & recovery -> Customer notification & follow-up.
We can provide: redacted timeline, sanitized logs, hit counts, and a summary of affected assets. For POCs we also include what dataset was used and whether any real customer data was present.

dave: Implementation note: for hosted POCs we can assemble and share a redacted incident timeline + artifacts (IDS alerts, request IDs, truncated logs). For Private/VPC installs the customer is typically the controller of notification unless contract says we respond; we need to check the POC agreement. :eyes: 

maria: For the RFP bundle let's put together: 1) one-page IR summary for customers, 2) a redacted excerpt of our IR playbook, 3) a sample notification template, and 4) notes on jurisdiction-specific timelines (GDPR, CCPA). I'll review the legal language before we share.

alicia: The POC is hosted and they used mainly synthetic data plus one sample CSV with emails and first names. I'll confirm exact fields and whether emails are real. Need the one-pager today if possible — customer asked for it before EOD.

ops-bot: Incident runbook (internal): https://wiki.redwood/infrasec/incident-response/poc-explainer — includes templates and artifact checklist.

samir: I'll draft the one-pager now with: notification window, what constitutes "confirmed" vs "suspected" incident, what artifacts we can share, and recommended customer actions. @maria will sign off on the wording.

maria: Also include: preservation hold instructions, secure artifact transfer options (SFTP/GPG link), and our security contact (secops@redwood) for the formal notification channel.

alicia: Great — I'm going to tell Acme we can provide an investigatory notice within 72 hours of confirmation and a redacted incident packet upon request. I'll update once I confirm the CSV fields. :thumbsup:

samir: FYI — for the packet we'll redact any unrelated tenant data and remove raw IPs where not necessary. We'll keep a sealed forensic copy for internal use.

dave: If you want a canned statement for the RFP we have a short paragraph we can use — I can paste it here once @maria gives the OK.

alicia: Perfect. Thanks team — will follow up after I hear back from the customer.
